plan.title: AD lesional vs control hallmark GSEA (Python)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks only which hallmark pathways are enriched in the treated (atopic dermatitis lesional skin) versus control contrast, and states that the DESeq2 differential expression results already exist. The plan therefore starts from /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns, gene symbol keyed) rather than refitting a model, and adds no unasked differential-expression scope.

Three steps. T1S1 is a sample-structure sanity check on the delivered Salmon count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv, with metadata.csv giving 6 treated vs 6 control): blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample library size and detected-gene counts. This exists specifically because the profile flags sample_01 at roughly 4x below the median library size — the enrichment inherits whatever that sample did to the delivered contrast, so it must be inspected and reported, not silently dropped. It is a check on the inherited input, not a re-analysis: no filtering, no refit, and no modification of de_results.csv.

T2S1 is the analysis that answers the question: preranked GSEA (gseapy.prerank, the Python equivalent of fgsea, per the user's Python-only constraint) over every tested gene in de_results.csv, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic. The Wald statistic is the stated side of the disputed ranking-metric rule: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, so it does not inflate low-count genes the way an unshrunken log2 fold change does, and it does not produce the mass ties of a signed p-value. The collection is the MSigDB human hallmark set, 2026.1, HGNC symbols — the same identifier space as the first column of de_results.csv, so no cross-space mapping is needed; the step reports the share of ranked genes that matched no hallmark set. Sets are restricted to 15-500 genes after intersection with the tested genes, and redundant significant sets are collapsed by leading-edge overlap.

T1S3 assembles the report: significant hallmark sets at FDR 0.05 with NES, leading-edge genes per set and their Wald statistics, the leading-edge overlap between reported sets, the collection version, the rank metric, the universe, the size window, the permutation seed, and the package versions. It states explicitly that the contrast direction is inherited from the delivered table (positive log2FC = higher in treated/lesional) and that enrichment results are method-dependent — a hallmark hit is a hypothesis, not a proven mechanism.

The environment carries the human hallmark GMT (2026.1) and gseapy 1.3.1, so the central step is executable. Reactome and WikiPathways would be the standard follow-up collections; only WikiPathways human (2026.07.10) is staged and no Reactome GMT is, so the plan keeps the follow-up optional in T2S1 and reports the two collections separately if run — never merged, since a pathway present in both is one finding tested twice.

steps.method: Sample structure QC in Python: pydeseq2 VST blind, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
gseapy preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1
Enrichment report with leading-edge genes, collection version, rank metric, universe, size window, reproducibility record
